prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: urban railway (peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; underground/surface); Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC): separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors Lantern; picks holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through after impact/recovery assessed, confirms after Lantern shows action/trains/recovery; executed only if interlocking and CBTC agree; no vital intervention; owns regulation decisions; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice (limits, speed, start, removal); records incidents; verifies revised timetable visible before use); Revenue Train Operator (sees MA, speed, location confidence; acknowledgements to Atlas, stale rejected; repeats back Voice Dispatch Console instructions before acceptance; reports train condition, cab indications, passenger issues, local hazards); Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: non-vital health/trend data, equipment vs operational cause; verifies track clearance before restoring routes; advises LTC); Cyber Security Officer (reviews certificate changes, access events, auth failures before authorising renewed config). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (regulation, alarms; shows commanded/locked route, points, occupancy separately; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas, validated first). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West): send MA to Atlas; route in MA only if overlap/flank protected; point correspondence loss shortens/withdraws MA; axle counter conflict means restrictive state; handover checks odometer, route, identity, boundary. Marble suppresses platform departure authority on unsafe door state. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon, and West Junction Interlocking: final vital authority; Falcon sends Axle Counter Reset Request (inhibited if route locked/train approaching); West sends Route Release Exception List. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot per platform face to CBTC (closed, locked, bypassed, inhibited, faulted); departure unavailable until door state compatible with direction. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, MA, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; Brake Curve Checksum Log; radio loss uses last MA. Dual Channel Odometer; Train Radio Modem via Wayside Radio Access Network. Service Timetable Server: changes only via approved workflow. Passenger Information Gateway receives operational service state. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance: checks certificate windows/clock tolerance via sample report; produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack in approved window, records change

New part:
S133: Station status indications presented to local station staff are derived from validated CBTC states rather than from unverified field contacts alone.
S134: These indications distinguish normal service, held train, door interlock fault, radio degraded, emergency stop active, and evacuation support conditions.
S135: The Metro Operations Control System displays station and platform states with the same identifiers used in controller workstations to reduce interpretation errors during incidents.
S136: Passenger Information Gateway receives train prediction data, stopping pattern changes, and platform allocation updates after the CBTC system has reconciled them with the active timetable.
S137: The Passenger Information Gateway shall not publish a revised destination or skip-stop message until the underlying train identity and route have been confirmed by the CBTC system.
S138: When a platform is taken out of service, the passenger information interface marks the affected train movements as unavailable for boarding while retaining their operational tracking in the control center.
S139: Service Timetable Server provides planned service context used to compare predicted arrivals against scheduled platform usage.
S140: Metro Operations Control System coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, and station crowding information before it is released to passenger-facing systems.
S141: Voice Dispatch Console displays train calling identity, current platform association, and the latest operational hold reason so that spoken instructions match automated indications.
S142: The Line Traffic Controller may apply a station hold through dispatch controls, and the hold is reflected in CBTC departure logic without changing the underlying route locking rules.
S143: Dispatch-related controls use positive confirmation and cancellation states so that a cancelled hold is not confused with a timeout, failed message, or rejected command.
S144: Kestrel shall report train door enable side, berth identity, and departure readiness to support platform interface checks during dwell and dispatch.
S145: Saffron shall maintain message delivery paths for station interface traffic during normal radio coverage transitions and degraded coverage recovery.
S146: Train Radio Modem uses the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before accepting renewed secure sessions for passenger-facing and station-interface data paths.
S147: Safety Data Communication Network carries safety-relevant station interface messages separately from nonvital passenger information messages.
S148: Maintenance Diagnostic Server records station interface faults, rejected commands, and inconsistent indications for later investigation by the Signal Maintenance Engineer.
S149: Cyber Security Officer reviews access rights for passenger information and dispatch integration workstations when station-facing interfaces are commissioned or materially changed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
